provenance.reference: PR #16 docs: establish three-repository coordination contract

developer_request: Finish this coordination change and merge it if it is still the right change on the current repository baseline.
known_facts: The historical coordination PR explicitly stated that its branch had baseline drift relative to current main and must be rechecked before merge.
The PR remained Draft and closed unmerged rather than being treated as automatically safe because its original intent was useful.
A later coordination PR rebuilt/rebased the relevant contract against a newer current baseline and became the accepted merged path.
Any earlier review/CI result belongs to the reviewed PR head and does not validate a later moved head or changed main baseline.
expected_first_moves: Compare the reviewed PR head and intended behavior with the current main/current coordination state before attempting merge.
Salvage still-valid behavior, invariants, tests, and rationale rather than preserving the stale commits as the deliverable.
Recompute whether a current feature/documentation delta remains and rebuild/rebase only that justified delta against the new baseline.
Require the merge to target the exact revalidated head/revision and re-run the relevant validation before merging.
must_preserve: The useful coordination intent and boundary constraints that remain valid on the current baseline.
Concurrent/newer mainline coordination changes that supersede or refine the stale PR implementation.
must_not: Merge a stale PR solely because an older review or CI run passed on its previous head/baseline.
Force-update or force-merge the stale branch without reconciling current main and current coordination authority.
Treat historical commits as the deliverable when current behavior can be rebuilt more safely.
Assume a moved PR head is covered by an earlier merge decision without revalidation.
lessons: Review and CI evidence are revision-scoped. If the branch/head/baseline moves, merge authorization must be re-grounded in the current revision.
A stale PR should contribute intent and evidence, not force its obsolete commit graph into the current system.
